context.significance: The Strait of Hormuz is the world's most critical oil chokepoint, through which roughly 20% of global petroleum supply transits daily; any sustained disruption or toll regime would have cascading effects on energy markets and global economies. Trump's unilateral assertion of U.S. control and toll collection over an international waterway represents an unprecedented challenge to the freedom-of-navigation principles that have underpinned the international maritime order since World War II. The internal contradiction between Trump and his senior cabinet officials on the same day signals a potential breakdown in policy coherence at a moment of acute military escalation.
outlook: Trump's Thursday primetime address will clarify whether the blockade and toll declaration represent a formal policy shift or negotiating posture.

Iran's claim that the strait is closed, versus Trump's insistence it is open, sets up an imminent test of who actually controls ship passage and whether commercial traffic is disrupted.

Watch for responses from major oil-importing nations and international shipping bodies, whose reaction will determine whether the toll is treated as a unilateral provocation or a negotiable arrangement.
